question: The band gap between conduction and valence band in metals is:
solution:
The correct answer is __0 eV**(metals)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Metals__ have a band gap of 0 eV between their conduction and valence bands.
 
• In metals, the conduction band and the valence band overlap, allowing free movement of electrons.
 
• This overlap explains the high electrical conductivity of metals.
 
• Unlike insulators or semiconductors, metals do not require external energy to excite electrons.
 
• The absence of a band gap is a key characteristic of metallic structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Insulators:**
 
 
• Insulators have a wide band gap, typically around 6.0 eV or more.
 
• This large band gap prevents the flow of electrons under normal conditions.
 
 
 
• **Semiconductors:**
 
 
• The band gap of semiconductors lies between 0.7 eV to 1.1 eV.
 
• Examples include silicon (1.1 eV) and germanium (0.7 eV).
 
• They require external energy such as heat or light to excite electrons.
 
 
 
• **Superconductors:**
 
 
• Superconductors exhibit zero resistance below a critical temperature.
 
• They are a special class of materials with unique quantum properties.
